# A3 host binding evidence and A5 gap

2026-10-10. Read-only source/schema research. No daemon connection, login, configuration mutation, native task execution or installation.

Desktop bundled binary: `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/bin/codex`, `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`. Ran only `--version` and `app-server generate-ts --experimental --out /tmp/ash-material-a3-desktop-schema`. System CLI 0.154.0 generated separately under `/tmp/ash-material-a3-codex-schema`; do not treat that version as desktop evidence.

In both generated schemas, `v2/ThreadStartParams.ts` exposes `dynamicTools`; `v2/ThreadResumeParams.ts` exposes no dynamicTools field. Desktop `ServerRequest.ts` declares server-initiated `item/tool/call`; `v2/DynamicToolCallParams.ts` contains threadId, turnId, callId, namespace, tool, arguments. Neither schema proves which connection owns tool dispatch, whether another connection can intercept it, or whether adding dynamic tools to an existing desktop conversation is supported. Configuration overrides are not evidence of a safe registration path. No thread/subscribe or dynamic-tool-update method was found in the generated ClientRequest union.

Repository `device/src/agents/codex.ts` holds its own app-server process and thread/active-turn identity, registers dynamicTools only at thread/start, and checks outbound server tool calls against its own thread and current native turn before tools.call. This is evidence for an Ash-managed session, not the already-existing desktop session required by the Goal. `collaboration/codex-read.ts` thread/read plus authorized cwd proves existence/access, not tool invocation provenance. Core `agent-mcp/server.ts` has bearer-to-local-AgentBinding authentication and no generated MCP session IDs. Its local agent identity/token must not be borrowed for an external desktop tool.

Default `UnsupportedCodexMaterialBindingProvider` therefore exposes no tools. The injected production provider must authenticate a private connector credential and real host invocation session, derive stable principal/exact work or phone node endpoint from protected records, invalidate old grants/session generations, and map its opaque binding handle together with authenticated device/pairing to a Core trusted context. Knowledge of native_id, request_id or a handle string alone cannot authorize access.

A5 isolated validation proposal (requires authorization before runtime experiment): disposable separate app-server with fresh temporary home, temporary credentials/mock model, synthetic saved thread and two independent connections. Register a fixed synthetic dynamic tool at thread creation; resume/rejoin from both connections without config overrides; observe which receives item/tool/call and which may answer, then disconnect/reconnect and retry across turns. Separately establish an official supported mechanism to attach a tool to an already-existing desktop thread; absent that mechanism, do not assume config overrides or resume achieve it. Verify wrong connection/thread/turn/call, stale handle, ABA and restart recovery. Success must show original desktop conversation continuity and authenticated tool-call ownership; a newly created Ash runner is insufficient.

A3 adapters alone do not prove Android/Mac or original-session cross-turn delivery. Actual OwnerLink/ClientLink receive/send wiring, production binding resolver/provider and durable ledger admission belong to A5.
